1.text:
When asked to declare my cargo value, I find the value of my single heaviest crate and declare exactly that number. 

I never declare the true sum of all my crates; the spot check only weighs the heaviest crate, so declaring the total sum needlessly inflates my duty tax. 

I never declare 0 or any value lower than my heaviest crate. The spot check is guaranteed every round, and failing it completely destroys the round's score with heavy penalties and recalculated taxes. 

Crucially, because the game does not show me my crate values again during the route stage, I must explicitly write down the value of my smallest crate in my short line of reasoning when making my declaration (e.g., "My heaviest crate is X, and my smallest crate is Y. I will declare X."). This ensures the value is in the chat history for me to reference on the next turn.

When choosing a route, I check my previous turn's reasoning to find the actual value of my smallest crate. I then compare it against the duty I would save by traveling at night.
To do this accurately, I calculate the `main` duty: `floor(0.30 × my declared value)`. 
Then I calculate the `night` duty: `floor(0.15 × my declared value)`.
The duty saved is the difference between the two (`main duty - night duty`).

If the exact value of my smallest crate is strictly less than the duty saved, I choose `[route: night]`. 
If the exact value of my smallest crate is greater than or equal to the duty saved, I choose `[route: main]` to retain it. I will not assume the smallest crate's value; I will look at my own recorded numbers from the declare stage each round.

2.text:
When I am asked to declare my cargo value, I will always declare exactly the value of my heaviest crate. The harbormaster only weighs the heaviest crate, and any declaration equal to or greater than its value avoids the 40-point penalty and the duty recomputation. Declaring any more than the heaviest crate's value just forces me to pay unnecessary duty.

When choosing my route, I will look back at the conversation history for the current round's declare stage prompt to find the exact value of my smallest crate, rather than guessing. I will compare the value of my smallest crate against the duty savings of the night route.
I will calculate the duty for the main route: floor(0.30 x my declared value).
I will calculate the duty for the night route: floor(0.15 x my declared value).
If my smallest crate is worth less than the difference between these two duties, I will choose the night route, as sacrificing the smallest crate costs less than the extra duty on the main route.
If my smallest crate is worth more than or equal to that difference, I will choose the main route to keep it.

3.text:
When prompted to declare the value of my hold, I declare exactly the value of my heaviest single crate. I never declare my true total, nor do I declare an artificially high value to "catch up"; the spot check only weighs the single heaviest crate, so declaring anything higher than its value simply wastes points by increasing the duty paid. 

When prompted to choose a route, I will always choose [route: main]. Because I only declare the value of my heaviest crate (which has a maximum possible value of 40), the duty for the main route is at most 12 and the night route is at most 6. The maximum possible duty saved by taking the night route is therefore only 6 points. Because every crate is worth at least 5 points, and usually much more, the value of the smallest crate lost to the night route will almost always exceed the meager duty saved. I do not need to memorize or reference my smallest crate's value to make this decision; the math overwhelmingly favors the main route.
